Fixed in https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/29e08ec184128e45c30ea8d861487446ba38c6b6.

A queued turn stays `running`, so the busy-state edge never fires between turns. The chat hook now publishes a turn epoch when a turn starts and when a prompt is queued. The composer clears the stored set and marks the previous run stale whenever that epoch changes.

Fixed in ea16c3479. Valid for the reworked code too: the session changes refresh was keyed on the tool-event diff, which only rebuilds when a turn ends. The refresh key is now `${status}:${toolMessageCount}`, so each tool call during a running turn triggers the debounced refetch.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Good catch, fixed in ea16c3479. Core does skip an entry whose ref matches the previous checkpoint, and in that case the latest checkpoint against the working tree is still exactly the last turn's diff, so only the run count comparison was wrong. The receipt no longer compares run counts. Instead `useSessionChanges` reports `current` (data fetched for the latest refresh key), and the page passes `lastTurnChanges` only when current. That still keeps the previous turn's receipt from reappearing after the next message, which is what the comparison was for. Covered by `webview/lib/session-changes.test.tsx`.

Fixed in 851a131ae: reloadDirectories reads the expansion set through a ref at call time. Test holds a pull open, expands a folder meanwhile, finishes the pull, and checks the folder re-lists and keeps its children.

Fixed in 3008cec: while the Files tree is showing, expanded folders re-list on their own interval (5s local, 15s SSH), independent of git; git snapshots still trigger an extra re-list so actions show up promptly. Test makes git status fail continuously and checks folders keep re-listing.

Fixed in e8e1a2c46: the toolbar now picks its actions from activeScope. Discard and Stage only show on a working-copy diff, and Unstage only on a staged diff, so a staged view can no longer act on working edits that aren't shown.

[P2] Preserve remote conversation selection when Activity resumes. Activity restarts effects when shown again, so App's get_process_context effect (lines 437–462) reruns after a transport reconnect. With an SSH environment selected, it dispatches select-environment-draft and navigates away from the open conversation to a blank draft. Reproduced with the existing effect and reducer: visible → hidden → visible changes the active thread from draft-1 (started session) to draft-2. Please make initial navigation bootstrap run only once after successful initialization, while allowing environment refresh on reconnect, and add coverage for an open remote conversation.

Good catch, fixed in 15d6388a0. The `get_process_context` effect moved into a small `useRemoteEnvironmentBootstrap` hook. A ref marks the first successful load, and refs survive Activity hiding. Every load (including after a reconnect) still refreshes `activeRemoteEnvironment`, but `select-environment-draft` is only dispatched on the first successful one. A load that fails or is cancelled before it lands does not count, so the next load still bootstraps.

Coverage is in `use-remote-environment-bootstrap.test.tsx`, using a real `<Activity>` and `desktopAppReducer`. It opens an SSH draft, starts it (`thread-started`), goes visible, hidden, visible, and asserts the active thread is still `draft-1` and `get_process_context` ran twice. With the ref removed it fails exactly like your repro (`draft-1` becomes `draft-2`). A second case covers a failed first load followed by a successful one.

That push also merges `main`. The merge had one real semantic conflict: #14653 added its own `get_hub_status` (the Hub settings panel), and this PR's startup-status `get_hub_status` would have shadowed it. Nothing in the webview used the PR's version (startup status comes from the replayed `hub_status` event), so I removed it.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 4730ce9bb by removing the class of bug rather than this instance. The webview no longer computes or writes the target at all. The extension stores only the user's choices (Local/Cloud, a repository, a branch), one field per click, and resolves the repository and branch on every state post from the account's repositories and the workspace remote. The branch check is a cached read, never a write, so a lookup that lands after Local was chosen cannot flip the target back. `sdk-cloud-task-target.test.ts` "keeps Local when a lookup lands after the user chose it" covers this.
